A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GEM for parameter-efficient 3D segmentation. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments, data-efficiency evaluations, component ablations, attention visualizations, and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds ShapeNetPart and SparseUNet evaluations in Appendix B.

M1.justification: GEM's spatial convolutional adapter, latent-token context adapter, insertion equations, and token-sharing procedure remain unchanged. The added ReCon and SparseUNet applications do not document a new component or revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix B adds ShapeNetPart object-part segmentation, substantially extending coverage beyond scene semantic segmentation. The original indoor and outdoor benchmarks remain. The SparseUNet experiment uses the already represented ScanNet and ScanNet200 datasets.

E2.justification: The new ShapeNetPart comparison evaluates PointLoRA and PointGST against GEM on ReCon, adding specialized 3D PEFT comparators absent from v1's experiments. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds ReCon evaluation using class and instance mIoU, plus SparseUNet pre-training on ScanNet and fine-tuning on ScanNet200 under the cited MSC protocol. The retained experiments keep their existing splits, metrics, parameter budgets, and reported training settings.

E4.justification: The new SparseUNet comparison explicitly tests whether GEM's benefits extend beyond transformer backbones. The existing spatial/context component ablations, token-count and sharing analyses, tight-budget tests, and attention visualizations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests for its experiments. The new comparisons continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Two new comparisons extend the findings to object parts and convolutional backbones. Table 8 reports GEM at 84.02 class/85.8 instance mIoU, versus PointGST's 83.98/85.8 and full fine-tuning's 84.52/86.1. Table 9 reports GEM at 15.2 mIoU versus linear probing at 1.5 and LoRA at 13.2; its prose claim of a 4.6-point gain contradicts these entries. All original table results are retained.

T1.justification: The method equations and complexity arguments are unchanged. Equations 2–3 replace expanded attention expressions with equivalent Attn notation. No new assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about geometry-aware adaptation, combining local and global information, and competitive performance while updating approximately 1.6% of parameters. The appendix extensions do not redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds interpretations about applicability beyond transformers, attributes weaker convolutional outcomes to limited backbone capacity, and identifies large shape-analysis heads occupying approximately 20% of parameters as an efficiency limitation. The original parallelization and backpropagation limitations remain.

D1.justification: The abstract and Appendix A replace promised future code release with a statement of availability and an explicit repository link. Existing hardware, training-duration, default-rank, token-count, and inference-batch disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds GAPrompt, PointLoRA, ReCon, and ShapeNetPart references. It replaces the general ShapeNet citation and the negative-transfer survey citation with different works. Related-work coverage expands modestly while retaining the positioning around PEFT for large 3D scenes.

P1.justification: v2 corrects spelling and grammar, refines several analysis paragraphs, adds appendix subheadings and cross-references, and updates author, conference, and acknowledgement information. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8–9 and renumbers the original tight-budget Table 8 as Table 10. Figures 3–4 and existing tables are repositioned, and the author block is reformatted. Existing figure content and table structures are substantially preserved.

improvement.justification: The direct comparisons with specialized 3D PEFT methods, added backbone evaluation, and explicit code-access information provide modest validation and reproducibility gains while preserving the original evidence. Reporting inconsistencies limit those gains: the SparseUNet prose claims +4.6 mIoU although Table 9 implies +13.7, and its full-fine-tuning row lists only 0.05% learnable parameters. These issues reduce confidence in the new convolutional extension.
